links.outcome: Flesch reading ease and layperson understandability of LLM-simplified versus original radiology reports
links.effect: Flesch reading ease: GPT-4o 46±7, Llama-3-70b 44±6, Mixtral-8x22B 44±6 vs original 17±13 (p<0.001); understandability 4.1-4.4 vs 1.5 (p<0.001).
links.quote: All three LLM reports yielded markedly higher layperson-understandability ratings than the original reports (GPT-4o: 4.4 ± 0.1; Llama-3-70B: 4.3 ± 0.1; Mixtral-8x22B: 4.1 ± 0.1 vs. 1.5 ± 0.1; p < 0.001 for each), with no significant difference between GPT-4o and Llama-3-70B (p = 0.136).

links.outcome: Errors with potential for patient harm in LLM-simplified radiology reports
links.effect: Mixtral-8x22B and Llama-3-70B produced more errors with potential for patient harm than GPT-4o (p = 0.005 and p = 0.025, respectively).
links.quote: Mixtral-8x22B and Llama-3-70B produced more errors with potential for patient harm than GPT-4o (p = 0.005 and p = 0.025, respectively).

unlisted_practices: Deploying open-weight LLMs on-premises in hospital for privacy compliance versus commercial closed-weight models

screen.reason: The study compares different LLM models (closed vs open-weight/on-premises) for simplifying radiology reports for laypersons; it evaluates model performance and readability rather than testing a specific implementation guardrail or deployment practice.
